name: Cable Hammer Curl
description: The cable hammer curl is a biceps and brachialis exercise using a cable machine with a rope attachment, performed with a neutral (palms-facing) grip. The neutral grip activates the brachioradialis to a greater degree than a supinated grip and maintains constant cable tension throughout the arc, unlike dumbbells. This variation effectively builds the outer arm thickness and brachialis definition.

execution.starting_position: Attach a rope to the low pulley of a cable machine. Stand facing the machine, holding each end of the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Arms extended toward the cable.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a rope to the low pulley. Stand close enough to the machine that the rope is taut at full arm extension with the hands near the thighs.
steps: Step 1: Hold the rope ends with a neutral grip, arms fully extended toward the low pulley.
Step 2: Brace the core and keep the upper arms stationary at the sides.
Step 3: Exhale and curl the rope upward by bending the elbows, keeping the neutral grip throughout.
Step 4: Curl to full contraction, then inhale and lower back to full extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl; inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drift forward — keep the upper arms pinned at the sides
Supinating the wrists at the top — maintain neutral grip
safety_considerations: Keep the wrists neutral and in line with the forearm — avoid wrist flexion or extension
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the bottom; full curl at the top.
coaching_cues: Keep the pinkies up and grip the ends of the rope firmly
Elbows stay at your sides — they are the pivot point
